sentences.text: Hello and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
I'm happy you are here.
Today we will talk about Liechtenstein.
Liechtenstein is a very small, rich,
and peaceful country in Europe.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Are you ready?
Let's begin.
Where is Liechtenstein?
Liechtenstein is in Central Europe.
It is between Switzerland and Austria.
It has no sea.
It is a landlocked country.
It is one of the smallest countries in the world.
What is the capital city of Liechtenstein?
The capital city is Vaduz.
Vaduz is a quiet city with mountain views,
a castle, and museums.
It is also the home of the royal family.
Other towns include Sean,
the largest town,
Balzers, Treason, and Eshen.
How many people live in Liechtenstein?
Only about 40,000 people live in Liechtenstein.
It is a small country with a small population.
Most people live in small towns.
What language do people speak in Liechtenstein?
The official language is German.
People speak a local German dialect called Alamanic.
Many people also speak English, French, or Italian.
What is the weather like in Liechtenstein?
Liechtenstein has four seasons.
Spring, cool and fresh.
Summer, warm and sunny.
Autumn, with colorful year,
cold with snow, good for skiing.
The weather is similar to Switzerland and Austria.
What does Liechtenstein look like?
Liechtenstein has mountains,
part of the Alps,
green valleys and rivers,
forests, meadows, and villages.
It is a perfect place for hiking, skiing, and nature walks.
What animals live in Liechtenstein?
In the wild, you can see deer, foxes, and hares.
Birds like eagles, owls, and woodpeckers,
cows, sheep, and horses on farms.
The country works to protect nature and animals.
What do people eat in Liechtenstein?
Food in Liechtenstein is simple, fresh,
and influenced by Switzerland and Austria.
People eat bread, cheese, and meat.
Potatoes, vegetables, and soups.
Popular dishes, kesnupfels,
small pasta with cheese and onions.
Rusty fried grated potatoes.
Schnitzel, breaded and fried meat.
Apple strudel, sweet pastry with apple filling,
soups and stews, especially in winter.
What do people drink in Liechtenstein?
People drink water, clean and fresh from the mountains.
Milk, tea, and coffee, fruit juice.
Adults may drink wine or beer, often from nearby regions.
Wine from Liechtenstein is made in small vineyards.
What is life like in Liechtenstein?
Life in Liechtenstein is calm, safe, and organized.
People enjoy spending time with family.
Outdoor sports like skiing and hiking,
reading and music, celebrating traditions and holidays.
Many people work in business, banking, or tourism.
What are some holidays and traditions in Liechtenstein?
National Day, August 15th, with fireworks and a party at the castle.
Christmas with lights and markets.
Easter with eggs and family meals.
New Year's Eve with music and fireworks.
Local festivals with folk music, food and dancing.
People also enjoy Swiss and Austrian traditions.
Some fun facts about Liechtenstein.
It is one of only two countries in the world without an airport.
It is a principality ruled by a prince.
The country is very rich but also very small.
Liechtenstein has no army.
The national flag is blue and red with a gold crown.
Now you know many things about Liechtenstein.
You know where it is, what people speak, and how they live.
You learned about food, nature, and traditions.
Great job.
I am Emili.
Goodbye.
